title: Your brain has its own age.
deck: Risk of Alzheimer's disease, as your brain tests older
counter_caption: of 100 · your age, ranked by brain age

_provenance.paper: doi:10.1038_s41591-025-03798-1 · Oh et al. 2025, Nat Med · prospective cohort, plasma proteomic organ clocks, UK Biobank n=44,498, 2-17y follow-up
_provenance.axis: Sweep-only ruling (founder, 2026-08-22) + owned-axis rule: x = where a person's brain age ranks among people their age, 0-100. The paper defines extreme agers by age-gap z-score beyond ±1.5, which is mathematically the outer ~7% of a normal distribution — so 'tests youngest' plots at 3, the reference at 50, 'tests oldest' at 97. The counter counts rank among 100 peers, the established house axis (movement + steps reels). Genre model: datakatadka SEX HORMONES BY AGE (17.2K) — counter sweeping an owned number while the curve resolves.
_provenance.reference: 'Typical' (50) = a brain testing its age — HR 1.00 by definition, the comparator, not a reported estimate

claims.quote: whereas a youthful brain (HR = 0.26) provided protection that was similar to carrying two copies of APOE2, independent of APOE genotype.
having an especially aged brain posed a risk of Alzheimer's disease (hazard ratio (HR) = 3.1) that was similar to carrying one copy of APOE4,

_provenance.copy_grounding: 'Protection like the best genes' ← c2 ('similar to carrying two copies of APOE2'). 'Risk like the worst gene' ← c1 ('similar to carrying one copy of APOE4, the strongest genetic risk factor'). Region flags are places (THE YOUNG END / THE OLD END), details carry the gene story — marker values carry the figures, nothing restates them. Widths measured: region1 span 476px vs detail 360px; region2 span 344px vs flag 209px / detail 288px.
_provenance.reveal_test: Headline names the premise, withholds what a brain's own age does; the counter climbs through peer rank while the curve stays low through 'typical', then bends up hard — 3.1× lands at the sweep's end as the payoff. Region flags carry the gene comparison mid-run.
_provenance.cold_read: Axis is a named organ the viewer owns, positioned the way school percentiles are ('of 100 people your age'). No counts, no z-scores, no derived quantity on the frame.
_provenance.honesty: Three reported points; segments between are interpolation per the template contract — the low-flat-then-bend shape is drawn only through reported values. z↔percentile mapping is a mathematical identity, not a new estimate. Association in cohort data; APOE comparisons are the paper's own. Mortality trio (0.60/0.58/0.44) stays caption material.
